headline: High: Kestra can write and execute workflows against shared resources, creating dangerous conflict and cascading-action risks with dbt-core; prompt-injection and leakage are lower due to limited direct ingestion evidence.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented, but Kestra can read/write files and ingest stdin/stdout while dbt-core can call a data warehouse and emit artifacts. A prompt-injection path would require unusual copy/paste or file handoff, so the blast radius is limited. Uncertainty keeps this above none.
conditions: IF Kestra workflows ingest dbt-generated text as instructions via stdin/stdout or files, injection becomes actionable.
IF an operator manually copies dbt output into a Kestra task definition, malicious content can steer execution.
mitigations: Keep dbt outputs out of workflow definitions.
Use a strict template/allowlist for any copied text.
Disable ad hoc stdin/stdout handoff between the tools.
Review any file-based handoff before execution.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress; Kestra reads files and can send logs, inputs, variables, artifacts, and notifications to many external services. A shared workspace or copied artifacts could leak sensitive warehouse data in default operational use, though direct cross-agent sharing is not documented.
conditions: IF dbt artifacts or warehouse extracts are placed in Kestra /app/storage or /tmp, Kestra can forward them onward.
IF Kestra notifications or logs include dbt outputs containing sensitive rows, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Store dbt artifacts outside Kestra-managed paths.
Redact sensitive fields before handing outputs to Kestra.
Restrict Kestra notification payloads.
Turn off verbose logging for shared runs.
Use separate service accounts and workspaces.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra has write_filesystem, execute_shell, spawn_subprocesses, and broad network egress, while dbt-core can call a data warehouse. Even without a documented shared directory, the pair can contend over the same mutable warehouse or files if orchestrated together; uncertainty about the exact deployment should be treated conservatively.
conditions: IF both agents target the same warehouse tables or shared files without locking, concurrent writes can conflict.
IF Kestra launches multiple dbt runs in parallel, stateful artifacts can be overwritten.
mitigations: Serialize writes to shared tables.
Use per-run working directories.
Add explicit locking around dbt state files.
Disable parallel execution for overlapping jobs.
Separate mutable resources by environment.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra is an automation/orchestration system with email, Slack, PagerDuty, and cloud actions; dbt-core produces transformation outputs that Kestra can treat as workflow inputs. If Kestra trusts dbt outputs without verification, a bad model can cascade into downstream notifications or actions. This is a default-dangerous pathway.
conditions: IF Kestra uses dbt-produced artifacts or status flags as authoritative triggers, downstream actions can be wrong.
IF dbt output is promoted into a Kestra task without validation, errors cascade to notifications or cloud tasks.
mitigations: Add validation gates before downstream tasks.
Require schema checks on dbt outputs.
Route failures to a manual approval step.
Limit automation to read-only notifications.
Log provenance for every dbt-derived input.

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, while Kestra handles logs, inputs, variables, artifacts, and notifications and can send them to third parties like Slack, email, and cloud services. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch for the same data class, but no specific jurisdictional violation is documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is copied into Kestra logs or notifications, retention and residency controls may diverge.
IF warehouse data is exported through Kestra to a third-party service, compliance obligations can change.
mitigations: Exclude regulated fields from logs.
Disable external notifications for sensitive runs.
Set short retention on Kestra artifacts.
Use region-matched services only.
Review data-flow mappings before enabling new tasks.
